---
title: Visualizing syntax graphs with Mermaid
jupyter: arsgrammatica
---

[Mermaid](https://mermaid.ai) is a lightweight diagramming language that is easily used in many Markdown viewers and editors, web environments, the [https://mermaid.live](https://mermaid.live) mermaid editor, and others. 


```{python}
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import Markdown, HTML, display
```

## Start from the token graph

To compose a Mermaid diagram for a token graph, first [analyze a string or a passage](./analysis.qmd), or read in a [previously saved analysis](./saving-loading.qmd). In this example, let's assume we have read in a saved analysis and used `split_analysis_by_sentence` to get a list of sentences called `sentence_slices`. Each sentence pairs a list of verbal units with the syntactic graph of tokens, but to create the HTML views, we only need the graph.


```{python}
#| echo: false
analysis_file = "../quarto/sample_data/vulgate_genesis_tokenized_42_27.cex"

from arsgrammatica import (
  read_analyses,
  split_analysis_by_sentence
)
tokengraph, verbalunits, sentences, lm_infos = read_analyses(analysis_file)
sentence_slices = split_analysis_by_sentence(tokengraph, verbalunits, sentences)
```


```{python}
sentence_tokengraph, sentence_verbalunits = sentence_slices[0]
```


## Collect a plain-text view of the passage

```{python}
from arsgrammatica import tokengraph_to_text
plain_text = tokengraph_to_text(sentence_tokengraph)
```
```{python}
#| echo: false
display(HTML("<blockquote>" + plain_text + "</blockquote>"))
```



## Compose a mermaid diagram

Use `tokengraph_to_mermaid` to create a diagram of the syntax graph. It returns two values: a Mermaid diagram string, and a list of any warnings (e.g., an edge that got skipped).

```{python}
#| echo: true
from arsgrammatica import tokengraph_to_mermaid
diagram, warnings = tokengraph_to_mermaid(sentence_tokengraph)
```


```{python}
#| echo: false
display(Markdown(f"```{{mermaid}}\n{diagram}\n```"))
```

## Save a diagram

You can save the diagram to a file with `save_mermaid`.

```python
from arsgrammatica import save_mermaid
save_mermaid(diagram,"diagram.mmd")
```

## Options

- Both `tokengraph_to_mermaid` and `save_mermaid` accept one of Mermaid's orientation codes (`BT`, `TB`, `LR`, `RL`) in an optional `orientation` argument, with default value `BT` (bottom-to-top). Since the token graph is directed from subordinate to governing nodes, `BT` will result in root elements at the top, and `RL` will place root elements at the left of the diagram. 
- Set the `show_root` parameter to `False` to omit the hypothetical `root` node of a sentence.

```{python}
diagram_rl, warnings = tokengraph_to_mermaid(
    sentence_tokengraph, 
    orientation="RL",
    show_root=False)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
display(Markdown(f"```{{mermaid}}\n{diagram_rl}\n```"))
```

## Limitations


Mermaid's layout engine cannot enforce aligning nodes by rank. (You can think of *rank* as the syntactic depth of the node, like the generations in a family tree.) This kind of alignment can make the diagram of very complex sentences easier to read. If you want diagrams aligned by rank, you can use the open-source `graphviz` program: see
 "[Diagramming syntactic analyses](../tutorials/diagrams.qmd)".
